title: Intermittent latency investigation playbook and trace fallacies
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic runbook for investigating short-lived, intermittent latency spikes that affect inference latency percentiles (95th/99th) but do not result in full outages. It focuses on metric definitions, trace anchoring heuristics, dashboard artifacts to build, and a prioritized triage checklist. Goal is to reduce mean time to identify root cause to < 30 minutes for repeatable patterns and < 2 hours for novel events.

Context & why this is different:
- Many existing docs focus on broad observability hygiene; this one targets ephemeral, high-percentile latency excursions that often defeat naive sampling strategies.
- Emphasizes trace fallacies: incorrect assumptions you might make when following spans (see section below).
- Gives compact SQL/snippet examples and lightweight dashboard widgets for fast correlation.

Key definitions (consistent names to use in dashboards/alerts):
- request.latency.ms: end-to-end API duration measured at gateway (ingress -> response sent).
- internal.inference.token_ms: per-token processing time observed at serving runtime (summed over token loop).
- kvcache.hit_rate: ratio of prefix/KV cache hits to total requests (tenant-scoped).
- batch.size.avg: average batch size for the model shard handling the request.
- route.fanout.count: number of model calls / parallel fanout per user request.
- host.cpu_steal_pct: host-level CPU steal (for CPU-bound pre/postprocessing).
- grpc.retries.count: internal retries triggered by transient errors (can inflate latency).
- tenant.qps: tenant request rate (1m/5m).
- s3.latency.ms / blobstore.latency.ms: external artifact read times (model weights, cache misses).

Trace anchor attributes to capture (span tags):
- request_id (global)
- session_id or conversation_id (user-level)
- model_variant (e.g., redwood-v2-7b-q4)
- route_name (API route/handler)
- shard_id and backend_node
- batch_size and batch_queue_time_ms
- kvcache.status: HIT | MISS | STALE
- prefix_length_tokens
- tenant_id and tenant_tier (free/premium/dedicated)

Trace fallacies (common traps):
1) Fallacy: The slowest span contains the root cause.
   Reality: Latency can be emergent across many small spans (queueing, scheduling, GC, spinlocks). Look for cumulative tail across many spans.
2) Fallacy: One trace equals one problem.
   Reality: Similar symptoms can have different causes. Group traces by anchor attributes (model_variant, kvcache.status, backend_node) before concluding.
3) Fallacy: Sampling hides important tails.
   Reality: Head-based sampling misses rare high-latency traces. Use severity-weighted sampling or targeted sampling when p95/p99 alert triggers.

Prioritized triage checklist (quick path):
Step 0 — Confirm scope
- Check whether spike is single-tenant, route-specific, or global.
- Query: SELECT percentile(request.latency.ms, 99) by route_name, tenant_id, region over last 15m.
- If only one tenant -> check tenant.qps and recent config changes.

Step 1 — Correlate infra signals (2 min)
- Compare host-level noise: host.cpu_steal_pct, host.load1m, disk_iops, network_errs over same window.
- Check autoscaler events / burst capacity transitions.
- If host-level contention aligns, escalate SRE.

Step 2 — KV cache and model artifacts (5–10 min)
- Look at kvcache.hit_rate and per-tenant prefix_heatmap.
- If kvcache misses spike -> correlate with model weight reads (s3.latency.ms) and backend_node memory pressure.
- Quick SQL: SELECT count() AS misses BY backend_node WHERE kvcache.status = 'MISS' AND ts > now() - 15m

Step 3 — Batching and queuing (5–10 min)
- Check batch.size.avg and batch_queue_time_ms. A sudden drop in batch size with higher queue time suggests scheduling stalls or aggressive per-req timeouts.
- Check for fanout amplification: route.fanout.count unexpectedly > 1.

Step 4 — Retries and transient errors (3–5 min)
- Inspect grpc.retries.count and HTTP 5xx spikes. Retries often multiply apparent latency.

Step 5 — Model-level hotspots and kernel scheduling (10–30 min deeper dive)
- Correlate token-level timing: check internal.inference.token_ms distribution. If token_ms spikes at a particular position (e.g., token index 1) that suggests cold KV cache or cold kernel path.
- Pull traces grouped by model_variant + shard_id to detect per-shard jitter.

Suggested dashboard widgets (fast to add to operations dashboard):
- p50/p95/p99 request.latency.ms by route, stacked with kvcache.hit_rate as an overlay line.
- Heatmap: request.latency.ms kernelized by time-of-day vs tenant.qps.
- Scatter: batch_queue_time_ms vs batch.size.avg (color by model_variant).
- Top-5 backend_node p99 latency and their recent OOM/GC counts.
- Trace-sampler funnel: number of traces sampled by reason (error-triggered / p99-triggered / heuristic).

Sampling strategy recommendations:
- Default: reservoir sampling for low-QPS tenants, head-based for high-QPS.
- Tail protection: always enable p99-triggered trace capture for the route/model pairs that exceed p99 threshold.
- Severity-weighting: increase sample rate for traces with batch_queue_time_ms > 50ms or kvcache.status = MISS.

Alert tuning guidance (avoid noisy alerts):
- Alert p99 latency breaches with recovery window: trigger if p99>X for 5m and at least 3 distinct backend_nodes contributing.
- Combine signals: require p99>threshold AND grpc.retries.count increase OR kvcache.hit_rate drop to avoid false positives.

Hypothesis bank (quick ideas to try in order):
- KV cache thrash because tenant prefix churn after new rollout -> confirm by kvcache.status and recent rollout tag in traces.
- Autoscaler oscillation causing cold model restarts -> confirm with scaling events + higher s3.latency.ms.
- Per-node NUMA scheduling or GPU context eviction causing micro-pauses -> correlate with host.cpu_steal_pct and driver logs.
- External rate-limiter or upstream causing spike in retries -> correlate with grpc.retries.count and upstream 429/503.

Playbook for postmortem collection (if incident becomes persistent):
- Export top 500 p99 traces (include all anchor attributes) and save to S3 with tag incident-id.
- Capture node-level perf profiles (perf/ebpf) for suspected backend_nodes during window.
- Run statistical clustering on traces by anchor set to find latent subgroups.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add a lightweight tenant-level trace tag to identify customers that recently changed prompt templates? (Nora to follow up with SE team)
- Implement p99-triggered sampling hook in trace ingest (GH PR referenced above). (Liam owner)
- Validate that our current batch_queue_time_ms is instrumented at producer and consumer sides consistently. (Diego to audit)

Appendix: quick grep/snippet examples
- Query top offending routes (example for our metrics store):
  SELECT route_name, percentile(request.latency.ms, 99) AS p99
  FROM inference_requests
  WHERE ts > now() - 15m
  GROUP BY route_name
  ORDER BY p99 DESC

- Find traces with kv cache misses and high token time:
  SELECT trace_id
  FROM traces
  WHERE tags.kvcache = 'MISS' AND span.metrics.internal.inference.token_ms > 30
  LIMIT 200

Notes to self:
- Keep runbook short — operators want a 3–5 step checklist they can follow in escalations.
- We should automate the initial correlation queries as a single diagnostic endpoint (obs-diagnose) that returns a structured summary.

If you're reading this and have a new pattern/heuristic, paste it below and we'll add to the Hypothesis bank.
